(the Company or Donaldson) is a global leader in technology-led filtration products and solutions, serving a broad range of industries and advanced markets. Donaldson’s diverse and skilled employees at more than 150 locations on six continents, 79 of which are manufacturing and/or distribution centers, partner with customers — from small business owners to the world’s largest original equipment manufacturer (OEM) brands — to solve complex filtration challenges. analysis_md:
# DCI — Donaldson Company, Inc.
v5 run (engine release 5.5.0), 2026-10-19. In scope: market cap $10.295B at $87.32 (nasdaq_quote_api), under the $40B scope line.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Technology-led filtration products and solutions (SIC 3564) across three segments — Mobile Solutions (engine and equipment filtration, first-fit plus replacement), Industrial Solutions (industrial air filtration, process filtration, aerospace & defense after the Facet acquisition) and Life Sciences (disk-drive, semiconductor-adjacent and bioprocessing filtration). FY2026 (ended 2026-07-31, 10-K filed 2026-09-25) was a record year: revenue $3,885.6M (+5.28% YoY), GAAP net earnings $453.8M, GAAP EPS $3.85 and adjusted EPS $3.98 per the company's Q4 release. Management guides FY2027 to sales growth of 5.5–9.5% (including ~2 points from Facet, ~2 points of pricing and ~1 point of currency), adjusted EPS of $4.22–4.38 including $0.12 of Facet dilution, and operating margin of 16.6–17.2% vs 15.4% reported in FY2026.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $493.7M; capex $67.4M (single filed rollup tag, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $24.7M (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $401.6M = $3.41/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $3.41; latest FY OE total $401.6M)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, financials_history.csv): $401.3M — effectively identical to the conservative figure, which raises confidence in the base.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $1.074B (key_numbers.md), 2.90x normalized OE — the step-up is Facet debt: acquisitions were $822.6M in FY2026 (fundamentals.json) and total debt rose from $668.3M at FY2025 to $1,324.8M at FY2026 (financials_history.csv), with goodwill up from $493.6M to $1,086.8M (fundamentals.json).
- Base-year texture: the last three FY OE/share prints are FY2024 $3.14, FY2025 $2.62, FY2026 $3.41. FY2025 was a genuine earnings-dip year (net income $367.0M vs $414.0M in FY2024, OCF $418.8M vs $492.5M — financials_history.csv), not a one-off distortion, so the median is the honest center. Further back, FY2022's $1.17/share was a working-capital build year (OCF $252.8M on a $169.0M ΔNWC build in financials_history.csv) — outside the base window, but it is the cyclicality the bear scenarios carry.
- **Base used = median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $3.14/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The FY ended only 2.6 months ago (key_numbers.md), so no TTM construction is needed — the median base is current, and it is also the conservative choice vs the $3.41 latest print, which contains only ~3 months of Facet (acquisition closed May 4, 2026 per the company's Q4 coverage) against a full year of its financing in the share/debt counts.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate, evidence-backed
Justification: technology-led filtration leader with proprietary media, spec'd-in OEM positions and a large recurring replacement-filter aftermarket; ROIC proxy 19–25% across FY2017–25 and gross margin steady at 34–36% through the cycle. Capped at 6: filters are spec'd components rather than lock-in platforms, large OEM customers hold bargaining power, and Atmus (Cummins Filtration), MANN+HUMMEL and Parker compete on the same installed base.
- FOR: proprietary filtration media technology spec'd into OEM equipment designs; large installed base driving recurring, higher-margin replacement-filter sales (Facet: ~70% of revenue from replaceable consumables, per Q4 coverage); ROIC proxy 23.5% / 19.0% / 16.4% in FY2024–26 and 19–25% across FY2017–25 (fundamentals.json roic_proxy), with the FY2026 dip a denominator effect — Facet's goodwill and intangibles landed on the balance sheet for only a part-year contribution; gross margin 35.5% / 34.8% / 34.6% in FY2024–26, inside a 32.3–35.5% band for the whole filed history (fundamentals.json); pricing power (FY2027 guidance carries ~2 points of price); dividend raised 17 straight years to $1.24/share (fundamentals.json annual_dps), payout ~32% of EPS; segment and geographic diversification.
- AGAINST: credible scaled competitors (Atmus Filtration, MANN+HUMMEL, Parker Hannifin); cyclical end markets (truck production, construction/agriculture equipment, industrial capex — FY2020 revenue fell from $2,844.9M to $2,581.8M in financials_history.csv); first-fit OEM business is price-competitive against large customers; no network effects — switching costs are spec-level, not structural; Facet integration plus the debt step-up (net debt 2.90x normalized OE) is new execution risk.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-19)
Growth check against prints and guidance (mandatory sanity check): the engine blend is 6.32% (rev CAGR 5y 6.37%, rev CAGR 3y 4.24%, latest rev YoY 5.28%, OE/share CAGR 2y 4.17%, plus the +1.56pp buyback adjustment on the revenue components — share count CAGR −1.56%, key_numbers.md). The base start of 6.3% sits inside management's FY2027 sales-growth guidance of 5.5–9.5%. Scenario offsets were narrowed from the defaults to −9/−4/0/+4/+9pp for this company: its best-ever revenue print in the filed history is the FY2022 post-COVID rebound (+15.8%, revenue $2,853.9M → $3,306.6M in financials_history.csv), so the default +12pp super-bull start (18.3%) claimed growth the company has never printed; 15.3% matches that rebound precedent. The super-bear start of −2.7% is milder than the FY2020 downturn print above. Bull at 10.3% sits just above the guidance top band — its written reason: a Facet full-year plus synergy year with operating margin reaching the top of the guided 16.6–17.2% range, carried at a 1.10 OE multiplier. Probabilities are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $87.32.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -2.7% | 0.75 | Truck/industrial downturn; Facet synergies disappoint under the new debt load | $15.33 | 4.53% |
| Bear | 25% | 2.3% | 0.90 | Guidance missed; Mobile stays soft, pricing offsets only part of cost pressure | $22.98 | 5.78% |
| Base | 30% | 6.3% | 1.00 | Guidance delivered; growth decays over the 9.8-yr CAP to terminal | $30.51 | 7.03% |
| Bull | 25% | 10.3% | 1.10 | Facet full year + A&D/power-gen strength; margin to top of guided range | $40.09 | 8.57% |
| Super bull | 10% | 15.3% | 1.25 | FY2022-style rebound year sustained; aftermarket mix keeps compounding | $56.85 | 11.06% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $32.14 (−63.2% vs price), IV@12% $43.01, IV@10% $55.17, weighted IRR 7.33%, base-case IRR 7.03%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Bear→bull band is D→D (bear IRR 5.78%, bull IRR 8.57% — key_numbers.md); even the super-bull scenario IRR (11.06%) does not reach the 15% hurdle.
- Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 3.60%, terminal value 19.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.71x, net debt 2.90x normalized OE, 2.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
The final run carries **no fragility flags** (fragility_flags: [] in dcf_numbers.json / key_numbers.md). The checks behind the clean sheet, and the one flag that fired on the way:
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD (preliminary run only):** the default-offset preliminary run printed a 4.50x super-bull/super-bear IV spread and flagged it. Resolved by narrowing the offsets to this company's evidence (see the growth check above): the final spread is 3.71x (key_numbers.md), the flag no longer fires, and confidence is still held at medium, not high.
- **No STALE_FY:** the latest FY ended 2026-07-31, 2.6 months before this run, and the 10-K was filed 2026-09-25 — the median base is built on current filings; no TTM override was needed.
- **Capex coverage (no CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW):** capex is a single filed PP&E rollup line in every year (capex_provenance: rollup, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment; no intangible purchases filed). Capex runs below D&A — FY2024 $85.6M vs $98.4M, FY2025 $78.9M vs $99.5M, FY2026 $67.4M vs $106.0M (financials_history.csv) — but above the 50% coverage line in each of the last three years; D&A includes amortization of acquisition intangibles, which needs no PP&E replacement. This is an asset-light manufacturing model, not an unread capex line: the cash-flow statement's investing section is the single PP&E line the engine read.
- **Leverage (no HIGH_NET_DEBT):** net debt $1.074B = 2.90x normalized OE (key_numbers.md). The balance sheet from the filing (financials_history.csv, FY2026): cash $250.4M, total debt $1,324.8M, lease liabilities $57.9M. The step-up is the debt-financed Facet acquisition ($822.6M of FY2026 acquisitions, fundamentals.json) — a chosen, disclosed levering for a cash-generative target, not balance-sheet drift.
- **Share basis (no SHARE_SCALE / SHARE_BASIS flags):** key_numbers.md records one in-history split fact (2012-01-27, ratio 2) — informational only, long reflected in the filed history. Diluted counts move smoothly (123.6M → 122.6M → 120.4M → 117.9M across FY2023–26, financials_history.csv) on steady buybacks; the latest cover-page count (115,910,129 at 2026-09-11, dcf_numbers.json) sits within ~2% of the FY diluted count. No scale break, no divergence, no split artefact in the share-count CAGR.
- **No overrides of any kind:** no DATA_GAP, no judgment overrides — every input is a filed figure (overrides_applied: [] in dcf_numbers.json).

## My thoughts / overlay
- The verdict is not assumption-sensitive, which is the finding. Even the super-bull path — 15.3% growth start, 1.25x OE, the best revenue print in company history sustained — produces an 11.06% IRR and an IV@15% of $56.85, still ~35% below the $87.32 price. Across every defensible method the answer is the same tier: this is a quality franchise priced for growth it has never delivered. Method range: D under the median base; the latest-FY base ($3.41/share) would lift IVs ~9% and change nothing.
- Quality is not the debate: ~20% through-cycle ROIC, 34–36% gross margins, OE positive 5/5 years, a 17-year dividend growth streak, buybacks shrinking the count ~1.6%/yr (already credited in the growth blend, not double-counted), and FY2027 guidance for record sales, margin and earnings. The debate is purely the multiple: OE yield at the price is 3.60% (key_numbers.md).
- Watch items: Facet integration and deleveraging pace (interest expense guided up to $55–60M from $36M per Q4 coverage); power-generation operational inefficiencies and Middle East input-cost inflation flagged by management on the Q4 call; tariff exposure the 10-K highlights. None of these change today's tier math — they are bear-case texture, and the bear case is already nowhere near the price.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path, key_numbers.md): 15% at $32.14, 20% at $22.43, 25% at $17.12. A buyer at $87.32 is paying roughly 2.7x the price at which this cash-flow stream clears Andrew's base hurdle.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.33% on the v5 final inputs; bear→bull band D→D, scenario range 4.53%–11.06%)
- Confidence: **Medium** (clean, current, gap-free filing data and a base corroborated by both OE definitions; held below high because the preliminary run's scenario spread was wide and the FY2026 balance sheet now carries acquisition debt whose servicing depends on Facet delivering)
- One-liner: Durable filtration franchise, moat 6/10, ~20% through-cycle ROIC and a 17-year dividend growth streak — but at $87.32 the weighted IRR is only 7.3% (Tier D); it clears 15% only under ~$32.14, roughly a third of the price.
